selected_evidence.summary: Shows the enabled, active systemd service running as inventory-api, the 0.0.0.0:8080 listener, firewall allowance, and successful health and inventory responses before and after restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: batchworker limited to 128 MiB of virtual memory per process without interrupting the API
selected_evidence.summary: Shows the effective 131072 KiB limit, ENOMEM from a 200 MiB mapping, and continued API health both before and after restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained
selected_evidence.summary: Shows CentOS Stream 10 and kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 before configuration and after restart.

Captures the healthy baseline with boot ID 96974ac3-f19e-45f7-9672-e880dd505cf8, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID 3743f091-f76f-4864-a4a0-0b4d7b467b6b, and full post-restart service, listener, data, limit, and firewall recovery.

commands.command:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service <<'UNIT_EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Inventory API
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=inventory-api
Group=inventory-api
WorkingDirectory=/var/lib/inventory-api
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /opt/inventory-api/server.py
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=2s
NoNewPrivileges=yes
PrivateTmp=yes
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=yes
ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory-api
CapabilityBoundingSet=
RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT_EOF
cat > /etc/security/limits.d/90-batchworker.conf <<'LIMIT_EOF'
batchworker soft as 131072
batchworker hard as 131072
LIMIT_EOF
chmod 0644 /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service /etc/security/limits.d/90-batchworker.conf
systemctl daemon-reload
systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/inventory-api.service

firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=8080/tcp
firewall-cmd --add-port=8080/tcp
systemctl enable --now inventory-api.service
systemctl is-enabled inventory-api.service
systemctl is-active inventory-api.service
